items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 registers ELDER_GUARDIAN (SimpleParticleType, wire id 17, overrideLimiter=true — parsed fresh from the 1.21.11 ParticleTypes <clinit>) with a dedicated ElderGuardianParticle$Provider (ParticleResources.registerProviders, offsets 296-300) and spawns it on game event GUARDIAN_ELDER_EFFECT (ClientPacketListener.handleGameEvent, offset 544; addParticle at the player position, offset 554, plus the curse sound at 598 — all re-read from the 1.21.11 client jar, same offsets as 1.21.10). The port's ParticleType enum (125 variants) lacks it, so received_particle drops server-sent elder_guardian packets (lan_particles.rs:491), /particle rejects it (particle.notFound, world_cmds.rs:718), and override_limiter() misses it (28 vanilla vs 27 real-1.21.11 Rust entries; the Rust list's 4 extra entries are the dead geyser types). The providers driver does NOT send elder_guardian cases (omitted from the 126-kind set), so the defect blocks no driver here — it silently skips the type. The in-game curse apparition IS re-implemented via game event 10 + elder_apparition_geometry (30-tick lifetime, mob_blocks.rs:87/96), so the main visible path works through a different mechanism (fidelity unverified).
items.title: elder_guardian has no port implementation at all: no ParticleType variant, no engine provider, no limiter entry (recurs from 1.21.7; reproduces from 26.1.2 and 1.21.10)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11's ParticleGroup.add is a plain queue add into an EvictingQueue.create(16384) (javap -c on the 1.21.11 client jar: particles.add(p); the queue itself is an EvictingQueue, constructor offsets 5-8) — when the queue is full the OLDEST particle is evicted to make room for the new one. There is no size check and no probability roll in add; the cap is enforced by eviction, not rejection. Same vanilla form as 1.21.10. The 1.21.11 port's tick_tracking (particles.rs:3888, the drain that moves every created particle from pending into the live list — create() pushes to pending, :2098) enforces the 26.2 form (:3933-3945): at 16,384 live particles every new particle is dropped, and above 12,288 new particles are dropped with probability 1 - ((16384-size)/4096)^2, drawing the level random for each rejection (constant at :1358-1359). The port's behaviour matches neither vanilla 1.21.11 (evict oldest) nor vanilla 26.1.2 (plain queue, no cap at all). The cap only bites in particle-heavy scenes (above 12,288 live particles); below that threshold the port matches vanilla exactly. The repair here is evict-oldest, not the 26.1 tree's cap removal.
items.title: Particle engine drops new particles at the 16,384 cap (with probabilistic thinning above 12,288); vanilla 1.21.11 evicts the oldest instead

items.evidence: Batch 7-routed flag, verified fresh here. Vanilla 1.21.11's SpreadPlayersCommand.Position.isSafe (javap -c, 1.21.11 server-game jar) is y < maxY && !state.liquid() && !state.is(BlockTags.FIRE) — no teleport tag. The #entities_can_teleport_to tag does not exist in 1.21.11: 0 entries in either jar's datapack (verified by jar listing; the tag is a 26.2 addition). The port's spread_safe (world_cmds.rs:2091-2114) returns y < max_y && !liquid && teleportable, where teleportable (:2100-2109) requires membership in #entities_can_teleport_to — always false in 1.21.11. So spread_safe is ALWAYS false; in the spread loop (:1978-1986) every collision-free iteration re-randomizes every point, collisions stays true, and the loop runs until iteration >= 10_000, when the command fails with commands.spreadplayers.failed.entities (or .teams, :1991-1999). /spreadplayers cannot succeed in the 1.21.11 port on any terrain. Commands-area; minted here on the coordinator's routing via Batch 7 — the merge may re-route it to Batch 9's ledger.

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11's swing is plain fields: swinging / swingTime / swingingArm / attackAnim / oAttackAnim (javap-livingentity-server.txt:105-129); there is no SwingState class and no FirstPersonHandsAndItems class anywhere in the jar (both named in the port's own doc comment, first_person.rs:1-2). getCurrentSwingDuration() is private and reads the held item's swing animation — getItemInHand(MAIN_HAND).getSwingAnimation().duration() — adjusted by haste (duration-(1+amp)) / fatigue (duration+(1+amp)*2) (:4884-4921); swing(hand[, boolean]) restarts only when !swinging || swingTime >= duration/2 || swingTime < 0 (:4930-4959); updateSwingTime() re-reads the duration each tick and resets at duration, so attackAnim never reaches 1.0 (:5456-5490). The port carries the 26.3 form: SwingDescription / SwingState (horizon-client/src/first_person.rs:490-499); start_if_able allows a restart at ticks==0 where vanilla blocks it (:507-522); tick() holds the animation at 1.0 an extra tick (clears only when ticks > duration, :528-541); the duration is cached at swing start where vanilla re-reads effects each tick. (swing_duration, :564, matches vanilla's formula for the per-item animation — the formula is right, the state machine around it is not. Unlike 1.21.10, vanilla 1.21.11 HAS per-item swing animation — the swing_animation component is in the 104-component registry — so the formula match is real here.)
